A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same four-stage counterfactual-reasoning framework and benchmark. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, and added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations across 11 datasets, including decompositional-task scores and experiments with tools and prompting strategies in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations and additional end-to-end, mediator-recall, and model-scaling results in Section 4.2.3 and Appendices B.3–B.4.

M1.justification: The four-stage framework, specialized tools, and CoT/CoT-SC/ToT procedures remain intact. Section 4.2.3 adds joint application of tool-assisted explicit-variable identification and prompted implicit-variable reasoning in an end-to-end pipeline, extending their separately evaluated use in v1.

E1.justification: The original 11 datasets, modalities, and worked examples remain. Appendix B.3 adds an Open-Critic-based n-back mediator-recall scenario requiring inference from causal variables presented one to three steps earlier, extending the tested temporal-dependency requirements.

E2.justification: The main comparison replaces GPT-4o, Qwen-VL, and Llama-3.2-11B with GPT-5/o4, Qwen3-VL, and Llama4 Scout/Maverick. Tables 4–5 also add Qwen to the auxiliary-technique comparisons. Gemini-Pro becoming Gemini2.5 is not independently counted as a new comparator: v1's reference already identifies Gemini 2.5 Pro.

E3.justification: V2 retains the ground-truth-conditioned, stage-isolated evaluations but adds end-to-end comparisons of explicit-only, implicit-only, and combined improvements. New protocols vary mediator-recall distance from one to three hops and Qwen-VL size across 2B, 4B, and 8B. Existing F1/accuracy metrics and shared sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether the two improvement strategies combine effectively in final predictions (Table 6), how mediator reasoning depends on recall distance (Table 10), and whether model scaling alleviates explicit and implicit reasoning difficulties (Table 11). These substantially extend v1's diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Across-instance standard deviations already appear in v1's Tables 2–3; v2 separates them into Appendix Tables 8–9. This relocation and the changed numerical deviations do not establish a new uncertainty-estimation practice. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and Figures 3–6 replace or extend results for the revised model panel, while Tables 6, 10, and 11 add combination, recall-distance, and scaling outcomes. For example, v2 reports GPT-o4 mediator-recall F1 of 72.2%, 63.5%, and 9.7% at one, two, and three hops. Results for replacement models are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The causal-variable definitions, DAG formulation, mediator/outcome functions, and counterfactual composition in Section 3.1 are retained. Added structural-causal-model motivation and citations introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a decompositional framework, an 11-dataset multimodal benchmark, identification of reasoning bottlenecks, and targeted auxiliary improvements. The additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations involving accumulated pipeline errors, working-memory constraints, model capacity, and modality-specific failures. It also removes v1's explicit limitations concerning simplified causal structures, auxiliary-tool errors, and untested application domains, rather than relocating those qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix A replaces the concrete CRASS JSON prompt and mandatory edge list with a universal four-task template containing intermediate ground-truth inputs and output fields. V2 also drops the explicit manual-curation wording. Hardware and shared query hyperparameters are retained, with v1's Appendix C moved to v2's Appendix B.1.

R1.justification: A new related-work passage explicitly distinguishes the framework from MalAlgoQA, DICE, CausalProbe, and other evaluations. V2 also expands its grounding in structural causal models and connects mediator difficulties to prior working-memory research. These additions substantially extend the research positioning beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and dataset examples remain closely matched. V2 expands introductory motivation, edits preprocessing explanations, corrects wording, adds subsections, and consolidates experimental appendices. The author list and conference header also change, but the main narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: The main result tables are restructured for seven models, with means and standard deviations separated between the main text and appendix. Figures 3–6 are redrawn with expanded series and legends, and new tables display the added analyses. The conference template and placement of figures and tables also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful end-to-end, memory, and scaling evidence, but introduces unresolved numerical inconsistencies and removes substantive limitations. For example, v1's Llama-3.2 CRASS exposure baseline and tool gain are 74.8 and +16.5; v2's Llama4-S values are 88.5 and +15.2, implying F1 above 100 on the reported scale (Tables 2 and 4). The added analytical value and these reliability and transparency losses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
